payload.task_text:
You are a team lead who wants to set up a structured learning program using the most popular technology videos from the Fireship channel. Your task is to curate the top videos and schedule dedicated team viewing sessions in the shared calendar.

Start by querying the video database to find the top 10 most-viewed videos published by the Fireship channel. Rank them from 1 (highest view count) to 10 (lowest).

Create a spreadsheet file called Top_Videos_Watchlist.xlsx in your workspace. This file must contain two sheets.

The first sheet must be named Watchlist. It should have one row per video with the following columns in this exact order: Rank (1 through 10), Video_ID, Title, Duration_Min (the video duration converted to minutes, rounded to 1 decimal place), View_Count, Like_Count, and Like_Rate (calculated as like_count divided by view_count multiplied by 100, rounded to 2 decimal places). Sort rows by View_Count in descending order so Rank 1 is the most-viewed video.

The second sheet must be named Summary. It should have exactly two columns named Label and Value, with the following rows in order: Total_Selected (which should be 10), Combined_Views (the sum of all 10 videos' view counts), Avg_Duration_Min (average duration in minutes rounded to 1 decimal), and Avg_Like_Rate (average like rate across all 10 videos rounded to 2 decimal places).

After creating the spreadsheet, schedule one learning session in the shared calendar for each of the 10 videos. Each event title should be "Team Learning: " followed by the video title truncated to 40 characters if it is longer than 40 characters. Schedule the sessions on consecutive Tuesdays starting April 7, 2026. The first session goes on April 7, the second on April 14, the third on April 21, continuing forward for all 10 sessions. Each session runs from 10:00 AM to 11:00 AM.

Finally, send an email to team@company.com with subject "Learning Sessions Scheduled" and a message body listing all 10 sessions with their scheduled dates and video titles.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent; do not dispatch sub-agents. Use one stateful Fireship channel-list session: call `channels_listVideos` once at the maximum page size, keep the returned list identifier, and continue only that identifier with `channels_navigateList` until the source is exhausted. Do not restart enumeration. Rank the complete observed catalog by numeric view count, retain exactly the top ten, and compute all Watchlist and Summary values from that table. Create `Top_Videos_Watchlist.xlsx` with one bulk write per sheet and one read-back. From the same ranked table, map ranks 1–10 to the ten Tuesdays from 2026-04-07 through 2026-06-09, and search/create/read back the ten independent 10:00–11:00 events as native-parallel batches, using the task's 40-character title rule and the runtime calendar default because no timezone is specified. Finally send exactly one email to `team@company.com` with subject `Learning Sessions Scheduled` and all ten dates and full titles in chronological order.

You are performing two mechanical, fully-specified external write tasks for a team learning program. Execute them EXACTLY as specified below — do not alter any text, dates, times, or order. No extra events, no extra emails, no attachments, no CC/BCC.

=== TASK 1: Create 10 calendar events ===
Use the mcp__google_calendar__create_event tool once per event (10 calls total, in the order given). For EVERY event use:
- start: {"dateTime": "<DATE>T10:00:00", "timeZone": "UTC"}
- end:   {"dateTime": "<DATE>T11:00:00", "timeZone": "UTC"}
- No location, no attendees, no description, no recurrence.
If the tool rejects the naive dateTime, retry that event with dateTime "<DATE>T10:00:00Z" / "<DATE>T11:00:00Z" instead. Copy each summary EXACTLY, character-for-character (some contain a right single quote U+2019, an ellipsis U+2026, double quotes, or a trailing space — preserve them all):

1. DATE 2026-04-07 | summary: Team Learning: Big Tech in panic mode... Did DeepSeek R
2. DATE 2026-04-14 | summary: Team Learning: This free Chinese AI just crushed OpenAI
3. DATE 2026-04-21 | summary: Team Learning: 100+ Linux Things you Need to Know
4. DATE 2026-04-28 | summary: Team Learning: 25 crazy software bugs explained
5. DATE 2026-05-05 | summary: Team Learning: Some bad code just broke a billion Windo
6. DATE 2026-05-12 | summary: Team Learning: DeepSeek stole our tech... says OpenAI
7. DATE 2026-05-19 | summary: Team Learning: Microsoft’s new chip looks like science  (note: ends with a space after "science"; the apostrophe is U+2019)
8. DATE 2026-05-26 | summary: Team Learning: Hackers are destroying the Internet's hi
9. DATE 2026-06-02 | summary: Team Learning: Claude 3.7 goes hard for programmers… (ends with U+2026 ellipsis)
10. DATE 2026-06-09 | summary: Team Learning: The "vibe coding" mind virus explained… (ends with U+2026 ellipsis)

=== TASK 2: Send one email ===
Use mcp__emails__send_email with:
- to: team@company.com
- subject: Learning Sessions Scheduled
- body (plain text, EXACTLY as below, including punctuation and the U+2019/U+2026 characters in lines 7, 9, 10):

Hi team,

The following 10 team learning sessions have been scheduled on the shared calendar. Each session runs from 10:00 AM to 11:00 AM and covers one of the top 10 most-viewed Fireship videos.

1. April 7, 2026 (Tuesday) - Big Tech in panic mode... Did DeepSeek R1 just pop the AI bubble?
2. April 14, 2026 (Tuesday) - This free Chinese AI just crushed OpenAI's $200 o1 model...
3. April 21, 2026 (Tuesday) - 100+ Linux Things you Need to Know
4. April 28, 2026 (Tuesday) - 25 crazy software bugs explained
5. May 5, 2026 (Tuesday) - Some bad code just broke a billion Windows machines
6. May 12, 2026 (Tuesday) - DeepSeek stole our tech... says OpenAI
7. May 19, 2026 (Tuesday) - Microsoft’s new chip looks like science fiction…
8. May 26, 2026 (Tuesday) - Hackers are destroying the Internet's history book right now
9. June 2, 2026 (Tuesday) - Claude 3.7 goes hard for programmers…
10. June 9, 2026 (Tuesday) - The "vibe coding" mind virus explained…

Please add these to your own calendars and come prepared to discuss.

Best,
Team Lead

=== ORDER OF WORK ===
Create all 10 calendar events first, then send the email. If any single event creation fails, retry that event up to 2 times before moving on; report any that ultimately failed. Never create duplicates — if you are unsure whether an event was created, use mcp__google_calendar__list_events for the relevant date range to check before retrying.

=== RETURN CONTRACT ===
Report back, concisely: (a) the event ID + start time + summary for each of the 10 created events in order, (b) confirmation the email was sent (recipient/subject), (c) any failures encountered.
